nodes.label: Can the long-session V6 plan be trusted before major implementation?
nodes.text: Freshly re-audit the long-session roadmap for context rot before expanding beyond the minimal kernel.

nodes.label: Original locked future architecture
nodes.text: The original plan locked a small portable kernel plus Microsoft-first/AWS-later runtime direction, later assurance/context/topology/model-seating work, and the #2→#3→#4/#7 implementation floor.

nodes.label: Stable vendor-independent invariants survive
nodes.text: Keep project-current-truth ownership, V6 authoritative control/evidence/lifecycle semantics, external-provider non-authority, FOSSIL durable-knowledge ownership, GitHub/CI merge independence, external bootstrap qualification, and simpler-baseline falsification.

nodes.label: Future implementation choices reopened as hypotheses
nodes.text: Microsoft-first framework choice, generic AgentRuntime seam, generalized AssurancePlan/provider abstraction, exact role topology, FOSSIL context winner, and 3/30 retry constants must earn continuation through explicit experiments.

nodes.label: Prove the combined kernel before expansion
nodes.text: Integrate PR #23 and #24 behavior on one exact SHA and qualify the combined production path before later architecture work.

nodes.label: Separate framework and hosting portability axes
nodes.text: Microsoft Agent Framework is an application framework/orchestration candidate; AWS AgentCore is a managed hosting/runtime candidate. They are not peer replacements at one abstraction layer.

nodes.label: Move value and qualification gates earlier
nodes.text: Run independent kernel qualification and progressive simpler-baseline value gates before accumulating runtime, assurance, topology, context, or seating abstractions.

nodes.label: OpenCode is external bounded bootstrap execution only
nodes.text: OpenCode may execute one pre-granulated authorized packet in an isolated workspace or read-only role. It is not authoritative task state, project planner, recursive orchestrator, hidden model router, completion authority, or egress-policy bypass.

nodes.label: 600-second exact-model bootstrap transport target
nodes.text: The V6/OpenCode transport target is one 600-second model request ceiling with exact requested model identity and hidden cross-model fallback disabled. LiteLLM/OpenCode implementation remains unqualified until litellm-ckff-ops#24 closes with evidence.

nodes.label: External-model data egress is a separate authority
nodes.text: Repository read authority does not automatically authorize sending the same data to an external model; #30 owns classification, secret handling, and egress authority.

nodes.label: 3-probe/30-normal retry remains unqualified
nodes.text: The 3-probe/30-normal retry target requires V5 donor qualification, failure taxonomy, cumulative time/cost budgets, backoff/switch semantics, and generation fencing before native #19 policy.

nodes.label: Corrected near-term execution order
nodes.text: Review #21, then #22, integrate #23/#24 under #26, externally qualify the kernel and run Gate A, prove SSC runtime retirement, resolve framework/hosting architecture, qualify egress/transport/OpenCode bootstrap, qualify needed V5 donors, then expand later mechanisms one at a time.
